questions.question: Which of the following are valid subdomains of myapp.com?
options: api.myapp.com
staging.myapp.com
myapp.com.api
admin.myapp.com
myapp.api.com

questions.question: What is the difference between a domain registrar and a DNS provider?
options: They are the same thing — one company always handles both
The registrar is where you buy the domain; the DNS provider hosts your DNS records
The DNS provider is where you buy the domain; the registrar hosts DNS records
The registrar issues SSL certificates; the DNS provider routes email
There is no meaningful distinction between them

questions.question: A TTL of 3600 on an A record means:
options: The record expires after 3600 requests
Other servers may cache the record for up to 1 hour
The record must be refreshed every 3600 days
The record is valid for 3600 milliseconds
DNS propagation will complete in exactly 3600 seconds

questions.question: Which of the following are true about CNAME records?
options: They can be used for root domains
They map a name to another domain name rather than an IP address
They cannot be used for subdomains
www.myapp.com can use a CNAME pointing to myapp.com
They are used to specify mail servers

questions.question: What is the correct order of a DNS lookup when you visit a website for the first time?
options: Browser cache → OS resolver → root nameserver → TLD nameserver → authoritative nameserver
Authoritative nameserver → TLD nameserver → root nameserver → OS resolver → browser
OS resolver → browser cache → authoritative nameserver → TLD nameserver
Root nameserver → browser cache → OS resolver → authoritative nameserver
Browser → authoritative nameserver directly

questions.question: Which of the following are distinct roles in web infrastructure?
options: Domain registrar
DNS provider
SSL certificate authority
Hosting provider
Browser vendor

questions.question: What is the difference between a URI and a URL?
options: A URI includes the protocol and domain; a URL is just a path
They are identical terms with no distinction
A URL includes the protocol and domain; a URI is just a path identifier
A URI is used only in Spring Boot; a URL is used in browsers
A URL is always secure (HTTPS); a URI may be insecure

questions.question: Which DNS record types map a name directly to an IP address?
options: A Record
CNAME
AAAA Record
MX Record
TXT Record

questions.question: Why might a site not be accessible immediately after updating its A record?
options: The new server needs time to boot up
DNS resolvers around the world may still be serving the cached old record based on the previous TTL
The domain registrar must manually approve all A record changes
ICANN must update its global database first
The browser must be restarted before DNS changes take effect
